To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

capillary gas chromatograph-mass spectrometric analysis is an efficient method for identifying polychlorinated dibenzofurans and polychlorinated naphthalenes in samples of technical mixtures and in environmental samples.

the analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) by capillary column gas chromatography (GC) and capillary column gas chroma-tography-mass spectrometer (GC-MS) is limited by the fact that the separation of PAHs on metal capillary columns (WCO) coated with Apiez-on L and OV-1 is not satisfactory.
capillary gas chromatographymass spectrometry can be used to identify isomeric PCB congeners in technical mixtures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following points: (a) the development of capillary gas-chromatographic methods of analysis for PCBs, and (b) the use of mass spectrometry for the identification of isomers of PCBs.
the analysis of PCBs by capillary GC, GC-MS, and the development of a capillary GC-MS method for the analysis of PCB congeners.

the following: (1) the development of a capillary gas chromatographic method for the determination of PCBs; (2) the development of methods for the identification of PCBs; and (3) the development of an analytical procedure for the determination of individual PCBs in Aroclors and in technical mixtures of PCB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of capillary gas chroma-tography and capillary column mass spectrometry is a powerful tool for the identification of individual PCB components in ArocIors.
the application of capillary gas-chromatography-mass spectometry to the analysis of polynuclear aromatics is possible and that the results obtained are satisfactory.
capillary gas chromatograph-mass spectrometric analyses of PCBs are possible, but the method is not yet sufficiently developed to be of routine use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the analysis of PCBs is possible by capillary gas-liquid chromatography, but that mass spectrometry is necessary for identification.
the analysis of PCBs by capillary gas chromotography-mass spectometry can give a good characterization of the components in a mixture of PCBs.
the separation of the PCBs in Aroclors 1242 and 1260 by means of gas chromatography is not a problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of PCBs by capillary gas-liquid chromatography is possible, provided that certain precautions are taken.

the use of glass capillary columns coated with OV-1 and OV-101 is recommended for the separation of PCBs and the direct coupling of a glass capillary to a mass spectrometry is recommended for the analysis of PCBs.
the use of capillary gas-liquid chromatography and capillar gas chromatography-mas spectrometry is a promising technique for the analysis of PCBs.
